name: A10-0010/2025 – David McAllister – § 3, indent 5 – Am 66
title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – 2024 annual report
part_text: – the 2024 Enlargement Report on Serbia, presented by the Commission on 31 October 2024; reiterates its position that accession negotiations with Serbia should advance only if the country aligns with EU sanctions against Russia and makes significant progress on its EU-related reforms, in particular in the area of the ‘fundamentals’; reminds the Serbian authorities that the proper functioning of democratic institutions is at the core of Serbia’s EU accession process and the EU accession methodology; recalls in this context its position that the Serbian parliamentary and local elections held on 17 December 2023 deviated from international standards and Serbia’s commitments to free and fair elections; reiterates its serious concerns over these irregularities and the overall election environment, which fell below the standards expected of an EU candidate country; is highly concerned by the credible reports on the use of unlawful crowd control technology against demonstrators during the mass protests on 15 March 2025 in Serbia, which caused injury to a number of demonstrators; calls for a thorough, impartial and speedy investigation into the allegations of violence against demonstrators and of police misconduct during protests; urges Serbia’s political leadership to ensure constructive, inclusive dialogue across the political spectrum and to deliver on the necessary reforms for Serbia to progress on the path to EU accession; regrets the biased approach of the EU towards Serbia despite its year-long roll-back on the rule of law, democracy and fundamental rights, as well as its destabilising influence on the whole region;
